newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-LATE PENALTY SAVES DORTMUND FROM EMBARRASSING DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE PENALTY SAVES DORTMUND FROM EMBARRASSING DRAW.

text.p: A late penalty saved European Cup quarter-finalists Borussia Dortmund from an embarrassing draw at bottom club Freiburg in the German first division on Saturday.

With five minutes remaining reigning champions Dortmund seemed to be heading for a 1-1 draw with Freiburg who before Saturday had taken just 13 points from 20 games and look doomed to play second division football next season.
But veteran midfielder Michael Zorc's crisp strike from the spot in the 86th minute sealed a 2-1 victory for Dortmund who replaced Bayern Munich at the top of the Bundesliga.
Dortmund lead on goal difference only and Bayern have a game in hand. The Bavarians travel to Bayer Leverkusen for a fascinating top-of-the-table clash on Sunday.
Freiburg took the lead with a 24th minute goal from Uwe Wassmer. But their lead was shortlived, Dortmund's Ghana international Ibrahim Tanko equalising two minutes later.

But Borussia, who took a confident step towards the semifinals of the European Cup in midweek with a 3-1 victory over French side Auxerre, got out of trouble. Zorc's winner silenced the bitterly disappointed Freiburg crowd.
